---
title: "Hash passwords that Cloudflare Workers can verify"
description: "Drop when the pinned release hashes passwords that a deployed Worker can verify, in every runtime, and verifies hashes above 100,000 iterations on Workers."
---

<!-- Generated by `pnpm upstream export` from the patch's commit message on top of Payload v4.0.0-beta.3. Edit the commit, not this page. -->

Cloudflare Workers rejects PBKDF2 above 100,000 iterations, and Payload hashes
passwords with 600,000. On a deployed Worker, creating the first user and every
login fail with "iteration counts above 100000 are not supported". Local
workerd does not enforce the limit, so only a deployed Worker shows it.

Every runtime now hashes with 100,000 iterations, and the hash records its
parameters (pbkdf2-sha256-v2-i\<iterations>-l\<keyLength>:\<hex>). A user that
the CLI, a seed script or vite dev creates in Node.js logs in on a Worker.

A Worker derives a hash with more iterations, such as one that upstream
Payload made at 600,000, in JavaScript with @noble/hashes. That costs about
half a second of CPU, once: login rehashes any hash whose parameters differ
from the current ones.

100,000 iterations is below OWASP's recommendation of 600,000 for
PBKDF2-SHA256. Upstream PR 18276 caps the count only on Workers, so a hash
made in Node.js still fails there.

- **Patch:** `workers-pbkdf2-cap`, committed as `fix(payload): hash passwords that Cloudflare Workers can verify`
- **Upstream:** [payloadcms/payload#18276](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/18276)
- **Tests:** `pnpm --filter payload exec vitest run src/auth/strategies/local; PAYLOAD_DATABASE=sqlite pnpm test:int test/auth/int.spec.ts; log in on a deployed Worker (pnpm deploy:staging in e2e)`
- **Diff:** [`upstream/patches/0001-fix-payload-hash-passwords-that-Cloudflare-Workers-c.patch`](https://github.com/AdiRishi/offload-cms/blob/main/upstream/patches/0001-fix-payload-hash-passwords-that-Cloudflare-Workers-c.patch)
